questions.questionText: What does "naive" refer to in Naive Bayes?
options: The algorithm is too simple to be used in production
It assumes all features are conditionally independent given the class, which is rarely exactly true
It only works on numeric data
questions.correctAnswer: It assumes all features are conditionally independent given the class, which is rarely exactly true
questions.explanation: This simplifying (and technically inaccurate) independence assumption is what makes the probability calculation tractable, even though real features are usually correlated.

questions.questionText: Why is Naive Bayes a popular choice for text classification specifically?
options: It can only be used on text data
It handles high-dimensional, sparse feature spaces (like word counts) efficiently and needs relatively little data
Text data violates the independence assumption less than other data
questions.correctAnswer: It handles high-dimensional, sparse feature spaces (like word counts) efficiently and needs relatively little data
questions.explanation: Text turns into thousands of sparse word-count features; Naive Bayes' simple frequency-counting approach scales to this well and trains fast.

questions.questionText: What's a known weakness of Naive Bayes' predicted probabilities?
options: They tend to be poorly calibrated / overconfident, even when the final class prediction is correct
They can't be computed at all
They ignore the prior class frequencies
questions.correctAnswer: They tend to be poorly calibrated / overconfident, even when the final class prediction is correct
questions.explanation: Because the independence assumption is violated in practice, the multiplied probabilities tend to be pushed toward extremes — the ranking of classes is often right, but the actual probability values are less trustworthy.
